legacy-design-tools.pointResolutionPath: For a bare {lat,lng} POST (no address): brokeragePlaceBuildableEnvelope.ts handleBuildableEnvelope (line 604) -> situsFirstPreResolve returns {situs:null} immediately since address is null (line 554) -> resolveContext (line 212) takes the explicit-coords branch, no network call, pointConfidence='coordinates' -> queryGisLayerGeoJson({layer:'parcels', latitude, longitude}) at line 769 -> brokerageGisLayers.ts:641 txParcelProviderMode()==='county-gis' branch -> resolvePointCountyByPip (brokerageTxParcels.ts:554, bounded: static bbox candidate filter then one indexed DB query per candidate county via countyStoreContainsPoint, Promise.all) -> queryTxCountyParcelsGeoJson -> for Travis (txgio-store-backed, confirmed by adapterKey txgio:parcels:48453 in the live probe) -> queryTxgioParcelsGeoJson (txgioParcelStore.ts:410), a single indexed (countyFips,tileKey) query plus bbox pre-filter, feature-capped, then one batched CAD land-use join.
legacy-design-tools.mechanism read: Every query in this path is indexed and bounded (tile-key partitioning, feature caps, static bbox pre-filtering) -- structurally NOT the same defect class as the pre-fix radius-search hang (which was an unbounded statewide county IN-list seq-scan over 16M rows, fixed in PR #572 by bounding to overlapping counties + tile cells). No unbounded query was found on this path.
legacy-design-tools.rejected mechanism: Considered: the point-pin path itself is slow by construction (e.g. a missing index). Rejected: read the schema access pattern -- every filter (countyFips, tileKey, then the 4 bbox columns) is exactly the radius-search precedent's own indexed shape, and my 4 live re-probes all completed in 1.4-1.6s, consistent with a fast, correctly-bounded query, not a structurally slow one.
legacy-design-tools.accepted mechanism: DB connection pool contention / transient upstream slowness under concurrent writer load elsewhere in the shared Neon store (consistent with F11's other two hangs that same hour on unrelated routes -- PE facets 60s-then-1.9s, situs-search 502-cortex-timed-out-5000ms -- and with the project's own documented 'read-under-writer-load' precedent). Not something a query-shape fix (the radius-search remedy) addresses, because the query shape here is already sound.
legacy-design-tools.scoped fix: Per mission item 6's explicit size cap ('if larger than a bounded timeout plus a refusal, stop and report'): wrap the point-resolution sequence (resolvePointCountyByPip + queryGisLayerGeoJson) in handleBuildableEnvelope's explicit-coords branch with a bounded race against a declared timeout (target ~8s, under the ~10s gateway ceiling that is currently surfacing as a bare 504), returning a typed 503 {errorClass:'resolution_timeout', message} instead of letting the platform kill the connection. Will note as a known limitation in the close: a Promise.race timeout does not cancel the underlying DB query, so it stops the bare-504 symptom but does not by itself relieve pool pressure if the root cause is contention -- flagging this as leave_behind for a possible statement_timeout-level fix rather than silently presenting the HTTP-level guard as a complete fix.
